champion.axis: concreteness_imageability — Mean word length as morphological complexity proxy (Brysbaert et al. Concreteness Norms; Morphological Complexity Hypothesis: base roots are short/concrete, affixations are long/abstract)
champion.code:
import re
import numpy as np
from wordfreq import word_frequency

_WORDS = re.compile(r"\b[a-z]+(?:'[a-z]+)?\b")
_STOPS = set(("a an the and or but if then else of to in on at by for with from as is are was were "
    "be been being it its this that these those i you he she we they me him her us them my your "
    "his their our not no so do does did have has had will would can could should may might must").split())

def _tokenize(text):
    tokens = _WORDS.findall((text or "").lower())
    return [t for t in tokens if t not in _STOPS]

def _content_tokens(text):
    tokens = _tokenize(text)
    return [t for t in tokens if len(t) >= 3]

def concreteness_word_length(text, anchor):
    content = _content_tokens(text)
    
    if not content:
        return 0.5
    
    lengths = np.array([len(t) for t in content])
    mean_len = np.mean(lengths)
    
    # Calibration: typical concrete word ~5 chars, abstract ~9 chars
    # Linear scale [0,1]: short words (5) -> 1.0, long words (12) -> 0.0
    score = max(0.0, min(1.0, (9.0 - mean_len) / 4.0))
    return score

METRICS = {"concreteness_word_length": concreteness_word_length}
